checks.finding: All four tasks are Risk: high with tdd. T-001 to T-003 change admission, evidence binding and protected-entrypoint guards, which are sensitive surfaces under risk-classification-policy.md. Advisory: T-004 (CI wiring, run-all, registry, delivery evidence) reuses the identical Risk Rationale as the other tasks. It is conservatively high because it binds the registration-removal gate (TEST-013) and the exact-head merge evidence. Not a blocking over-classification.

Every task's Done When includes 'Record the task preflight, RED-to-GREEN regressions and disposable rollback test with exact hashes' and 'Independent diff review and formal quality evaluation have no blocking findings'. No task is Risk: critical, so no second-approver item is required.

T-001 Planned Files span more than three distinct implementation areas. They are launch/preflight/probe/guard scripts (py/mjs), the spec-review-precheck sh/ps1 pair, three SKILL.md files plus review-context-boundary.md, quality-loop validators/evaluator/quality-gate skill, and seven test suites plus a shell test. That is roughly 25 files across five or more areas in one session, covering AC-001 and AC-002 together (REQ-001, REQ-002). The failure mode is an unfinishable or partially verified task, since the preflight, RED evidence and rollback inventory are required per task. T-002 to T-004 are appropriately sized.
The functional ACs have error-path coverage. AC-001 has TEST-002 and TEST-003a-c. AC-002 has TEST-005a-h. AC-004 has TEST-008a-d. AC-005 has TEST-010a-b. AC-006 has TEST-012a-d and TEST-013.

The tasks reference ACs and TEST IDs rather than declaring a unit/integration/E2E type. The mapped tests are consistent with their scope. TEST-004 and TEST-006 are multi-component or CI-level, TEST-007 to TEST-010 are single-recipe checks, and each cites an AC.

The 'Rollback for every task' section requires a before-byte/hash inventory and a disposable-checkout restore of task-owned targets, with executed commands recorded. T-004 adds an isolated combined-revert test. Each high task's Done When also requires a disposable rollback test.

Shared files are ordered by Blockers and the scope-boundaries text. validate-review-context-set.{sh,ps1} appear in T-001 and T-002, and T-002 is blocked by T-001. host-review-preflight.tests.py appears in T-001 and T-003, and T-003 is transitively blocked by T-001. T-004 owns only the registration files.

T-002 needs T-001's released validators, and T-004 needs T-001, T-002 and T-003. Advisory: T-003's blocker on T-002 has no file or artifact dependency, since T-003 needs only T-001's test driver. It is justified by the stated single-owner serialization of canonical reservations (tasks.md line 10), so it is not treated as a spurious-blocker defect.
SKIP: no bugfix or debugging task in scope. All four tasks complete approved admission, normalization and registration portions of the existing candidate, and none is scoped as a bugfix.

findings.finding: T-001 (REQ-001, REQ-002; AC-001 and AC-002) lists about 25 Planned Files across five or more areas: launch/preflight/probe/guard scripts, the spec-review-precheck sh/ps1 pair, three SKILL.md files and the boundary reference, quality-loop validators/evaluator/quality-gate skill, and eight test files. That exceeds the three-implementation-area oversize indicator. Consider splitting it, for example into caller-argument/permission enforcement (AC-001) and ordered-input/receipt/reservation admission (AC-002). Otherwise the task cannot be completed and evidenced in one focused session.
